instruction: At the gate of the house of prayer that stands outside the village, under the threshold, by the door-post that has shifted: [deposit].
context: Redacted site description: an upland village built among ancient remains in a hilly region. Its best-known ruin is a large building of columns whose stone façade, with three doors, is partly used as a house; a columned porch stood in front of it. Rock-cut tombs are reported around the village.

features.type: rock-cut tomb with three vaulted chambers
features.notes: Reported by an earlier traveller among several tombs examined at the village; once a pilgrimage tomb.
Side door in the same façade, west of the main door (from the published plan).

features.type: columned porch in front of the façade
features.notes: Pedestals in place; double columns at the corners; one column still carries its architrave; the architrave over the central bay was probably raised to a point.
Side door in the same façade, east of the main door (from the published plan).

features.type: doorway with stone threshold (main door of a columned building)
features.notes: Main door of the almost complete stone façade; the doors now lead into a modern mud-and-stone house built against the ruin. Mouldings of the door posts drawn by the surveyors.

withheld_question: On which side of the chosen gate is the shifted door-post?
